skill.name: uniprot-database
skill.description: Direct REST API access to UniProt for protein searches, FASTA retrieval, ID mapping, Swiss-Prot and TrEMBL annotations, and field-specific data retrieval.
skill.summary: Query UniProt protein records, sequences, annotations, and identifier mappings through REST workflows.
skill.author: davila7

content.value_statement: Protein research often needs accurate sequence, annotation, and identifier data from UniProt. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through REST queries, FASTA retrieval, ID mapping, and field selection.
actual_capabilities: Search UniProtKB by protein name, gene, accession, organism, taxonomy, and GO term.
Retrieve individual protein entries in JSON, TSV, FASTA, XML, RDF, or text formats.
Map identifiers between UniProt and external databases such as Ensembl, RefSeq, PDB, KEGG, and GO.
Stream large result sets and batch retrieve accessions using the provided Python client.
Select specific UniProt fields for compact tabular or structured outputs.
Compare reviewed Swiss-Prot entries with unreviewed TrEMBL entries.
limitations: Requires network access to UniProt REST endpoints for live data.
Does not validate biological conclusions or replace expert curation.
Large mapping jobs can take time and are subject to UniProt service limits.
Returned records reflect UniProt availability and may change over time.

use_cases.title: Find Protein Records
use_cases.description: Search reviewed human protein records by gene, accession, organism, or functional terms before deeper analysis.

use_cases.title: Build ID Mapping Workflows
use_cases.description: Convert UniProt accessions into PDB, Ensembl, RefSeq, GO, or other database identifiers for downstream pipelines.

use_cases.title: Prepare Sequence Datasets
use_cases.description: Retrieve FASTA sequences or compact TSV fields for curated datasets, batch jobs, and reproducible analysis.

prompt_templates.title: Search Human Protein
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner search for a reviewed protein set.
prompt_templates.prompt: Search UniProt for reviewed human insulin proteins. Return accession, gene name, organism, sequence length, and a short function summary.

prompt_templates.title: Retrieve FASTA Sequence
prompt_templates.scenario: Retrieve a known protein sequence by accession.
prompt_templates.prompt: Retrieve the FASTA sequence for UniProt accession P01308. Explain which endpoint and format should be used.

prompt_templates.title: Map Protein Identifiers
prompt_templates.scenario: Map accessions into structure and genome databases.
prompt_templates.prompt: Map these UniProt accessions to PDB and Ensembl identifiers: P01308, P04637, Q9Y6K9. Include failed mappings if present.

prompt_templates.title: Design Batch Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow planning for larger UniProt datasets.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a UniProt workflow to collect reviewed human kinases, select compact TSV fields, handle pagination, and cache reusable results.

output_examples.input: Find reviewed human BRCA1 records with core fields.
output_examples.output: A concise table-style summary with accession, entry name, gene, organism, sequence length, and reviewed status.

output_examples.input: Retrieve the FASTA sequence for P01308.
output_examples.output: A FASTA-ready sequence result with the accession, protein name, organism, and sequence text.

output_examples.input: Map P01308 and P04637 from UniProt to PDB.
output_examples.output: A mapping summary that lists matched structure identifiers, missing mappings, and the UniProt job status.

best_practices: Use reviewed:true when manually curated Swiss-Prot records are required.
Request only needed fields to reduce response size and processing time.
Cache repeated queries and add delays for large batch jobs.
anti_patterns: Do not treat TrEMBL predictions as manually validated evidence.
Do not request complete streams when pagination or field selection is enough.
Do not submit sensitive unpublished identifiers unless external API sharing is acceptable.

faq.question: What does this skill connect to?
faq.answer: It uses the public UniProt REST API and related UniProt documentation.

faq.question: Can it retrieve FASTA sequences?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports FASTA retrieval for individual accessions and larger query result sets.

faq.question: Does it support ID mapping?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide mappings between UniProt and supported databases such as PDB, Ensembl, RefSeq, KEGG, and GO.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is marked compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it work offline?
faq.answer: No. Live searches and retrieval need network access to UniProt.

faq.question: Can it analyze biological meaning?
faq.answer: It can summarize UniProt annotations, but expert review is needed for scientific conclusions.
